decided: Concurrency and scaling coverage lands as NEW benchmark files beside the existing ones, never by editing them: emit/concurrency_bench_test.go (RunParallel Record accept/suppressed, InFlightTracker Track/Done contention, Publish scaling series, slow- and erroring-exporter back-pressure) and engine/compute_load_bench_test.go behind a //go:build benchload tag (Compute at 10k/100k/1M/2M events). The gate's benchmark set is unchanged in cost profile except for the cheap parallel additions; the multi-gigabyte Compute series is tag-excluded so scripts/ci-bench.sh's `go test -list` never sees it. Every published concurrency figure comes from `-cpu=1,2,4,8,18` sweeps, which benchstat already understands, rather than from bespoke goroutine plumbing. docs/performance.md carries methodology, tables, and an explicit limits section; README's Performance section shrinks to four headline figures linking there.
why: Three constraints pull against each other. (1) The bead forbids weakening BENCH_TIME/BENCH_COUNT or the gate, and ci-bench.sh runs `-bench .` over every module at count=6 — so any benchmark added to an untagged file runs six times on every PR. Compute at 1M events is ~3.2 GB of live heap and seconds per sample; on a 7 GB hosted runner that is an OOM, not a slow job. A build tag is the mechanism the bead explicitly authorises for exactly this, and it stays honest as long as performance.md says the series is excluded and prints the command. (2) The scaling question the founder asked ('is 2M 7.5 s or 75 s') can only be answered by measuring, so the tagged series must actually reach 2M rather than extrapolate. (3) Concurrency numbers must not depend on one goroutine outracing another: `-cpu` sweeps with RunParallel vary cores and goroutines together with no timing thresholds anywhere, and the one place where a race genuinely matters — does exporter back-pressure reach Record — is asserted by a deterministic test (a blocked exporter released only after the buffer is provably full), not by a timing benchmark. Editing the existing benchmarks instead of adding beside them would move their baselines, which the policy forbids.
cost_if_wrong: If the tag is the wrong call, the load series silently bit-rots: nothing in CI compiles a benchload-tagged file, so a refactor of engine.Compute or memq breaks it and no one learns until someone reruns performance.md's commands. That is a stated limit in the doc and a follow-up bead, not a hidden risk. If the parallel benchmarks turn out too noisy for benchstat at count=6 they will manufacture phantom regressions on unrelated PRs — the mitigation is that they are pure contention loops with no dataset construction inside the timed region, and their observed variance is reported in performance.md so a reader can judge. Cost of the inverse error (publishing only single-goroutine numbers, or fabricating a scaling curve from extrapolation) is a payments-path adopter sizing their deployment off a figure that does not hold under load.
alternatives: Add the 1M/2M Compute sizes to the existing untagged BenchmarkCompute — rejected: OOMs a 7 GB runner and multiplies gate wall-clock for a number no PR-vs-main comparison needs

Gate the heavy series behind an env var read at runtime (b.Skip when unset) instead of a build tag — rejected: `go test -list` still counts it, so ci-bench.sh reports a benchmark that always skips, and skip-green-on-an-opt-in is the shape the vacuous-pass rule polices

Drive the goroutine curve with bespoke sub-benchmarks that spawn N goroutines and divide b.N — rejected: reimplements RunParallel worse, produces names benchstat cannot fold into a -cpu comparison, and a hand-rolled work split is where a benchmark quietly stops measuring what it claims

Assert back-pressure with a timing threshold ('Record returned in under X ms while the exporter slept Y ms') — rejected outright: that assertion is blind under -race, the documented failure mode this session already hit on another branch; the blocked-exporter test either deadlocks or passes, with no threshold to be wrong about

Optimise the contention the numbers surface (shard emit.Std's mutex, shorten InFlightTracker.Publish's critical section) inside this PR — rejected: ADR-0015 orders correctness, then readability, then benchstat, and says the benchmark lands first; a regression these numbers surface is a finding to report, not scope to absorb
scope: New: emit/concurrency_bench_test.go, engine/compute_load_bench_test.go (//go:build benchload), docs/performance.md. Edited: README.md Performance section and its Documentation list, CONTRIBUTING.md Benchmarks section (one bullet naming the tagged series). Untouched: scripts/ci-bench.sh, .github/, .warden/, repo.yaml, graph.yaml, every existing benchmark function, and every non-test file under emit/ and engine/ — no production code changes in this PR. Out of scope by ownership: adapters/query/, docs/adapters.md, go.work, test/docsnippets/.
